paper.title: Joint Optimization and Variable Selection of High-dimensional Gaussian Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Variable selection of a high-dimensional GP sample (HDS)
unmapped: f is a sample from a zero-mean GP on [-1,1]^D with squared-exponential kernel depending only on an unknown set A of d active variables (d << D); goal is to identify A
the learner knows the kernel bandwidth b and self variance sigma_s^2
settings.definition_quote: Let f : [-1,1]^D -> R be a fixed, but unknown function. ... We assume that this function depends only on a subset of the domain variables, which we call the active variables ... we assume that the kernel is of the form K(x,x') = sigma_s^2 exp(-sum_{i in A}(x_i-x'_i)^2/b^2) ... y_t = f(x_t)+eps_t ... eps_t i.i.d. normal ... variance sigma^2 > 0 (assumed known)

settings.name_in_paper: Joint variable selection and GP optimization (cumulative regret)
unmapped: f is a GP sample on [-1,1]^D with squared-exponential kernel depending only on d unknown active variables
the learner knows the kernel bandwidth b, self variance sigma_s^2 and the number of active variables d (used in beta_t and delta)
settings.definition_quote:
We evaluate any candidate algorithm in

source.quote: Running HDS with FDT and recovery rate 1-\epsilon, followed by the GP-UCB algorithm on the variables deemed active guarantees that with probability \ge 1-\delta_o: E(R_T) \le A'_T\sqrt{T} + (N+1)C_0 + 2 + \frac{N C_0}{T}, where A'_T = \sqrt{C_1\beta_T\gamma_T} = O((\log T)^{d/2+1}), C_1 = 8/\log(1+b^{-2}), and N = O(\log(1/\epsilon)^9) = O((\log T)^9).
